body: NIST DLMF section 5.20 (Physical Applications) says: "In nonrelativistic quantum mechanics, collisions between two charged particles are described with the aid of the Coulomb phase shift \operatorname{ph}\Gamma\left(\ell+1+\mathrm{i}\eta\right) ; see ( 33.2.10 ) and Clark ( 1979 ) . Suppose the potential energy of a gas of n point charges with positions x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{n} and free to move on the infinite line -\infty<x<\infty , is given by The probability density of the positions when the gas is in thermodynamic equilibrium is: where k is the Boltzmann constant, T the temperature and C a constant. Then the partition function (with \beta=1/(kT) ) is given by For n charges free to move on a circular wire of radius 1 , For further information see Mehta ( 2004 ) . Veneziano ( 1968 ) identifies relationships between particle scattering amplitudes described by the beta function, an important early development in string theory. Carlitz ( 1972 ) describes the partition function of dense hadronic matter in terms of a gamma function." Equation 5.20.1 on the page has alt text "W=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}x_{\ell}^{2}-\sum_{1\leq\ell<j\leq n}\ln|x_{\ell% }-x_{j}|.". Equation 5.20.2 on the page has alt text "P(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})=C\exp\left(-W/(kT)\right),". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
